[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// Sets the number of worker-threads to use as `num_threads`.
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    /// Can be used to change the threadpool size during runtime.
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// Will not abort already running or waiting threads.
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    ///
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    /// # Panics
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    ///
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    /// This function will panic if `num_threads` is 0.
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    ///
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// # Examples
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    ///
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// ```
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    /// use std::time::Duration;
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    /// use std::thread::sleep;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    ///
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    /// let mut pool = ThreadPool::new(4);
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    /// for _ in 0..10 {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    ///     pool.execute(move || {
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    ///         sleep(Duration::from_secs(100));
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    ///     });
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    /// }
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    ///
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    /// sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for threads to start
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    /// assert_eq!(4, pool.active_count());
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    /// assert_eq!(6, pool.queued_count());
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    ///
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    /// // Increase thread capacity of the pool
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    /// pool.set_num_threads(8);
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    ///
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for new threads to start
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    /// assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    /// assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    ///
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    /// // Decrease thread capacity of the pool
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// // No active threads are killed
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    /// pool.set_num_threads(4);
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    ///
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    /// assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// ```
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    pub fn set_num_threads(&mut self, num_threads: usize) {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        assert!(num_threads >= 1);
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        let prev_num_threads = self
[573](https://docs.rs#573)            .shared_data
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            .max_thread_count
[575](https://docs.rs#575)            .swap(num_threads, Ordering::Release);
[576](https://docs.rs#576)        if let Some(num_spawn) = num_threads.checked_sub(prev_num_threads) {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)            // Spawn new threads
[578](https://docs.rs#578)            for _ in 0..num_spawn {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                spawn_in_pool(self.shared_data.clone());
[580](https://docs.rs#580)            }
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        }
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    }
[583](https://docs.rs#583)
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Block the current thread until all jobs in the pool have been executed.
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    ///
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// Calling `join` on an empty pool will cause an immediate return.
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// `join` may be called from multiple threads concurrently.
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    /// A `join` is an atomic point in time. All threads joining before the join
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// event will exit together even if the pool is processing new jobs by the
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// time they get scheduled.
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    ///
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// Calling `join` from a thread within the pool will cause a deadlock. This
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    /// behavior is considered safe.
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    ///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    /// # Examples
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    ///
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    /// ```
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    /// use std::sync::Arc;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    /// use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    ///
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    /// let pool = ThreadPool::new(8);
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// let test_count = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// for _ in 0..42 {
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    ///     let test_count = test_count.clone();
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    ///     pool.execute(move || {
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    ///         test_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    ///     });
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// }
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    ///
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    /// pool.join();
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    /// assert_eq!(42, test_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// ```
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    pub fn join(&self) {
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        // fast path requires no mutex
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        if self.shared_data.has_work() == false {
[618](https://docs.rs#618)            return ();
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        }
[620](https://docs.rs#620)
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        let generation = self.shared_data.join_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        let mut lock = self.shared_data.empty_trigger.lock().unwrap();
[623](https://docs.rs#623)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        while generation == self.shared_data.join_generation.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)            && self.shared_data.has_work()
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)            lock = self.shared_data.empty_condvar.wait(lock).unwrap();
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        // increase generation if we are the first thread to come out of the loop
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        self.shared_data.join_generation.compare_and_swap(
[632](https://docs.rs#632)            generation,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            generation.wrapping_add(1),
[634](https://docs.rs#634)            Ordering::SeqCst,
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        );
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    }
[637](https://docs.rs#637)}

[639](https://docs.rs#639)impl Clone for ThreadPool {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    /// Cloning a pool will create a new handle to the pool.
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    /// The behavior is similar to [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/sync/struct.Arc.html).
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    ///
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// We could for example submit jobs from multiple threads concurrently.
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    ///
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// ```
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// use std::thread;
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    /// use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    ///
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    /// let pool = ThreadPool::with_name("clone example".into(), 2);
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    ///
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    /// let results = (0..2)
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    ///     .map(|i| {
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    ///         let pool = pool.clone();
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    ///         thread::spawn(move || {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    ///             let (tx, rx) = channel();
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    ///             for i in 1..12 {
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    ///                 let tx = tx.clone();
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    ///                 pool.execute(move || {
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///                     tx.send(i).expect("channel will be waiting");
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    ///                 });
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///             }
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    ///             drop(tx);
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    ///             if i == 0 {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    ///                 rx.iter().fold(0, |accumulator, element| accumulator + element)
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    ///             } else {
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    ///                 rx.iter().fold(1, |accumulator, element| accumulator * element)
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    ///             }
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    ///         })
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    ///     })
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    ///     .map(|join_handle| join_handle.join().expect("collect results from threads"))
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    ///     .collect::<Vec<usize>>();
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    ///
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    /// assert_eq!(vec![66, 39916800], results);
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// ```
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    fn clone(&self) -> ThreadPool {
[677](https://docs.rs#677)        ThreadPool {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)            jobs: self.jobs.clone(),
[679](https://docs.rs#679)            shared_data: self.shared_data.clone(),
[680](https://docs.rs#680)        }
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    }
[682](https://docs.rs#682)}

[704](https://docs.rs#704)impl PartialEq for ThreadPool {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// Check if you are working with the same pool
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    ///
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// ```
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    ///
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    /// let a = ThreadPool::new(2);
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// let b = ThreadPool::new(2);
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    ///
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// assert_eq!(a, a);
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// assert_eq!(b, b);
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    ///
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// # // TODO: change this to assert_ne in the future
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    /// assert!(a != b);
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// assert!(b != a);
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// ```
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    fn eq(&self, other: &ThreadPool) -> bool {
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        let a: &ThreadPoolSharedData = &*self.shared_data;
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        let b: &ThreadPoolSharedData = &*other.shared_data;
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        a as *const ThreadPoolSharedData == b as *const ThreadPoolSharedData
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        // with rust 1.17 and late:
[725](https://docs.rs#725)        // Arc::ptr_eq(&self.shared_data, &other.shared_data)
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    }
[727](https://docs.rs#727)}
[728](https://docs.rs#728)impl Eq for ThreadPool {}
[729](https://docs.rs#729)
[730](https://docs.rs#730)fn spawn_in_pool(shared_data: Arc<ThreadPoolSharedData>) {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    let mut builder = thread::Builder::new();
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    if let Some(ref name) = shared_data.name {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        builder = builder.name(name.clone());
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    }
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    if let Some(ref stack_size) = shared_data.stack_size {
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        builder = builder.stack_size(stack_size.to_owned());
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    }
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    builder
[739](https://docs.rs#739)        .spawn(move || {
[740](https://docs.rs#740)            // Will spawn a new thread on panic unless it is cancelled.
[741](https://docs.rs#741)            let sentinel = Sentinel::new(&shared_data);
[742](https://docs.rs#742)
[743](https://docs.rs#743)            loop {
[744](https://docs.rs#744)                // Shutdown this thread if the pool has become smaller
[745](https://docs.rs#745)                let thread_counter_val = shared_data.active_count.load(Ordering::Acquire);
[746](https://docs.rs#746)                let max_thread_count_val = shared_data.max_thread_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
[747](https://docs.rs#747)                if thread_counter_val >= max_thread_count_val {
[748](https://docs.rs#748)                    break;
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                }
[750](https://docs.rs#750)                let message = {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)                    // Only lock jobs for the time it takes
[752](https://docs.rs#752)                    // to get a job, not run it.
[753](https://docs.rs#753)                    let lock = shared_data
[754](https://docs.rs#754)                        .job_receiver
[755](https://docs.rs#755)                        .lock()
[756](https://docs.rs#756)                        .expect("Worker thread unable to lock job_receiver");
[757](https://docs.rs#757)                    lock.recv()
[758](https://docs.rs#758)                };
[759](https://docs.rs#759)
[760](https://docs.rs#760)                let job = match message {
[761](https://docs.rs#761)                    Ok(job) => job,
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                    // The ThreadPool was dropped.
[763](https://docs.rs#763)                    Err(..) => break,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)                };
[765](https://docs.rs#765)                // Do not allow IR around the job execution
[766](https://docs.rs#766)                shared_data.active_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[767](https://docs.rs#767)                shared_data.queued_count.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[768](https://docs.rs#768)
[769](https://docs.rs#769)                job.call_box();
[770](https://docs.rs#770)
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                shared_data.active_count.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                shared_data.no_work_notify_all();
[773](https://docs.rs#773)            }
[774](https://docs.rs#774)
[775](https://docs.rs#775)            sentinel.cancel();
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        })
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        .unwrap();
[778](https://docs.rs#778)}

[831](https://docs.rs#831)    #[test]

# Builder in threadpool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/threadpool/1.8.1/threadpool/struct.Builder.html

`pub struct Builder { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html) factory, which can be used in order to configure the properties of the

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

`ThreadPool`The three configuration options available:

- `num_threads`: maximum number of threads that will be alive at any given moment by the built- `ThreadPool`
- `thread_name`: thread name for each of the threads spawned by the built- `ThreadPool`
- `thread_stack_size`: stack size (in bytes) for each of the threads spawned by the built- `ThreadPool`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Build a [ ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html) that uses a maximum of eight threads simultaneously and each thread has
a 8 MB stack size:

```
let pool = threadpool::Builder::new()
    .num_threads(8)
    .thread_stack_size(8_000_000)
    .build();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#570-582)#### pub fn [set_num_threads](https://docs.rs#method.set_num_threads)(&mut self, num_threads: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#570-582)

#### pub fn [set_num_threads](https://docs.rs#method.set_num_threads)(&mut self, num_threads: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Sets the number of worker-threads to use as `num_threads`.
Can be used to change the threadpool size during runtime.
Will not abort already running or waiting threads.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

This function will panic if `num_threads` is 0.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::time::Duration;
use std::thread::sleep;
let mut pool = ThreadPool::new(4);
for _ in 0..10 {
    pool.execute(move || {
        sleep(Duration::from_secs(100));
    });
}
sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for threads to start
assert_eq!(4, pool.active_count());
assert_eq!(6, pool.queued_count());
// Increase thread capacity of the pool
pool.set_num_threads(8);
sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for new threads to start
assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
// Decrease thread capacity of the pool
// No active threads are killed
pool.set_num_threads(4);
assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
```
Block the current thread until all jobs in the pool have been executed.

Calling `join` on an empty pool will cause an immediate return.
`join` may be called from multiple threads concurrently.
A `join` is an atomic point in time. All threads joining before the join
event will exit together even if the pool is processing new jobs by the
time they get scheduled.

Calling `join` from a thread within the pool will cause a deadlock. This
behavior is considered safe.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
let pool = ThreadPool::new(8);
let test_count = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
for _ in 0..42 {
    let test_count = test_count.clone();
    pool.execute(move || {
        test_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    });
}
pool.join();
assert_eq!(42, test_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
```

### impl [Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html) for [ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#676-681)[§](https://docs.rs#method.clone)#### fn [clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone)(&self) -> [ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#676-681)

[§](https://docs.rs#method.clone)

#### fn [clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone)(&self) -> [ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

Cloning a pool will create a new handle to the pool.
The behavior is similar to [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/sync/struct.Arc.html).

We could for example submit jobs from multiple threads concurrently.

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::thread;
use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
let pool = ThreadPool::with_name("clone example".into(), 2);
let results = (0..2)
    .map(|i| {
        let pool = pool.clone();
        thread::spawn(move || {
            let (tx, rx) = channel();
            for i in 1..12 {
                let tx = tx.clone();
                pool.execute(move || {
                    tx.send(i).expect("channel will be waiting");
                });
            }
            drop(tx);
            if i == 0 {
                rx.iter().fold(0, |accumulator, element| accumulator + element)
            } else {
                rx.iter().fold(1, |accumulator, element| accumulator * element)
            }
        })
    })
    .map(|join_handle| join_handle.join().expect("collect results from threads"))
    .collect::<Vec<usize>>();
assert_eq!(vec![66, 39916800], results);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#687-691)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Default-for-ThreadPool)### impl [Default](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/default/trait.Default.html) for [ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

Create a thread pool with one thread per CPU.
On machines with hyperthreading,
this will create one thread per hyperthread.

use threadpool::ThreadPool;
let a = ThreadPool::new(2);
let b = ThreadPool::new(2);

assert_eq!(b, b);

```

# threadpool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/threadpool/latest/threadpool/

## Expand description

A thread pool used to execute functions in parallel.

Spawns a specified number of worker threads and replenishes the pool if any worker threads panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#synchronized-with-a-channel)Synchronized with a channel

Every thread sends one message over the channel, which then is collected with the `take()`.

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
let n_workers = 4;
let n_jobs = 8;
let pool = ThreadPool::new(n_workers);
let (tx, rx) = channel();
for _ in 0..n_jobs {
    let tx = tx.clone();
    pool.execute(move|| {
        tx.send(1).expect("channel will be there waiting for the pool");
    });
}
assert_eq!(rx.iter().take(n_jobs).fold(0, |a, b| a + b), 8);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#synchronized-with-a-barrier)Synchronized with a barrier

Keep in mind, if a barrier synchronizes more jobs than you have workers in the pool,
you will end up with a [deadlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadlock)
at the barrier which is [not considered unsafe](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/behavior-not-considered-unsafe.html).

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::sync::{Arc, Barrier};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
// create at least as many workers as jobs or you will deadlock yourself
let n_workers = 42;
let n_jobs = 23;
let pool = ThreadPool::new(n_workers);
let an_atomic = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
assert!(n_jobs <= n_workers, "too many jobs, will deadlock");
// create a barrier that waits for all jobs plus the starter thread
let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(n_jobs + 1));
for _ in 0..n_jobs {
    let barrier = barrier.clone();
    let an_atomic = an_atomic.clone();
    pool.execute(move|| {
        // do the heavy work
        an_atomic.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        // then wait for the other threads
        barrier.wait();
    });
}
// wait for the threads to finish the work
barrier.wait();
assert_eq!(an_atomic.load(Ordering::SeqCst), /* n_jobs = */ 23);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- `ThreadPool`- `ThreadPool`
- [Thread](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)- Pool
- Abstraction of a thread pool for basic parallelism.

# num_cpus

Count the number of CPUs on the current machine.

## Usage

 = "1.0"
```
In your `main.rs` or `lib.rs`:

extern crate num_cpus;
// count logical cores this process could try to use
let num = get;
```
Count the number of CPUs on the current machine.

Add to Cargo.toml:

```
[dependencies]
num_cpus = "1.0"
```
In your `main.rs` or `lib.rs`:

```
extern crate num_cpus;
// count logical cores this process could try to use
let num = num_cpus::get();

# threadpool 1.8.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/threadpool/latest/source/CHANGES.md

#Changes##1.8.1*[Fix a typo](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/107)##1.8.0*[Raise minimal rustc version to 1.13.0](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/99)*[Update num_cpus to 1.13.0](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/105)##1.7.1*[Join waves](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/89)##1.7.0*[Introduce `threadpool::Builder`](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/83)*[Add more hyperlinks to documentation](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/87)*[Add keywords and categories to Cargo.toml](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/88)##1.6.0*[Implement `PartialEq` and `Eq` for `ThreadPool`](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/81)##1.5.0*[Implement `Default` for `ThreadPool` use 'num_cpus' crate.](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/72)##1.4.1*[Introduce `with_name`, deprecate `new_with_name`](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/73)*[Documentation improvements](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/71)##1.4.0*[Implementation of the `join` operation](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/63)##1.3.2*[Enable `#[deprecated]` doc, requires Rust 1.9](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/38)##1.3.1*[Implement std::fmt::Debug for ThreadPool](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/50)##1.3.0*[Add barrier sync example](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/35)*[Rename `threads` method/params to `num_threads`, deprecate old usage](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/34)*[Stop using deprecated `sleep_ms` function in tests](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/33)##1.2.0*[New method to determine number of panicked threads](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/31)##1.1.1*[Silence warning related to unused result](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/30)*[Minor doc improvements](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/30)##1.1.0*[New constructor for specifying thread names for a thread pool](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/28)##1.0.2*[Use atomic counters](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/25)##1.0.1*[Switch active_count from Mutex to RwLock for more performance](https://github.com/rust-threadpool/rust-threadpool/pull/23)

# num_cpus 1.17.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/num_cpus/1.17.0

# num_cpus

Count the number of CPUs on the current machine.

## Usage

Add to Cargo.toml:

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
In your `main.rs` or `lib.rs`:

```
extern crate num_cpus;
// count logical cores this process could try to use
let num = get;
```
Count the number of CPUs on the current machine.

Add to Cargo.toml:

```
[dependencies]
num_cpus = "1.0"
```
In your `main.rs` or `lib.rs`:

```
extern crate num_cpus;
// count logical cores this process could try to use
let num = num_cpus::get();
```

# num_cpus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/num_cpus/1.17.0/target-redirect/num_cpus/

## Expand description

A crate with utilities to determine the number of CPUs available on the current system.

Sometimes the CPU will exaggerate the number of CPUs it contains, because it can use
[processor tricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simultaneous_multithreading) to deliver increased performance when there are more threads. This
crate provides methods to get both the logical and physical numbers of cores.

This information can be used as a guide to how many tasks can be run in parallel. There are many properties of the system architecture that will affect parallelism, for example memory access speeds (for all the caches and RAM) and the physical architecture of the processor, so the number of CPUs should be used as a rough guide only.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Fetch the number of logical CPUs.

`let cpus = num_cpus::get();`See [ rayon::Threadpool](https://docs.rs/rayon/1.*/rayon/struct.ThreadPool.html) for an example of where the number of CPUs could be
used when setting up parallel jobs (Where the threadpool example uses a fixed
number 8, it could use the number of CPUs).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [get](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html)
- Returns the number of available CPUs of the current system.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_physical.html)- physical
- Returns the number of physical cores of the current system.

# ThreadPool in rayon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rayon/1.*/rayon/struct.ThreadPool.html

`pub struct ThreadPool { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Represents a user-created [thread pool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thread_pool).

Use a [ ThreadPoolBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPoolBuilder.html) to specify the number and/or names of threads
in the pool. After calling

[, you can then execute functions explicitly within this](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPoolBuilder.html#method.build)

`ThreadPoolBuilder::build()`[using](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

`ThreadPool`[. By contrast, top-level rayon functions (like](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html#method.install)

`ThreadPool::install()``join()`) will execute implicitly within the current thread pool.[§](https://docs.rs#creating-a-threadpool)Creating a ThreadPool

[ install()](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html#method.install) executes a closure in one of the

`ThreadPool`’s
threads. In addition, any other rayon operations called inside of `install()` will also
execute in the context of the `ThreadPool`.When the `ThreadPool` is dropped, that’s a signal for the threads it manages to terminate,
they will complete executing any remaining work that you have spawned, and automatically
terminate.

Use `ThreadPoolBuilder::build`

Deprecated in favor of `ThreadPoolBuilder::build`.

Executes `op` within the thread pool. Any attempts to use
`join`, `scope`, or parallel iterators will then operate
within that thread pool.

[§](https://docs.rs#warning-thread-local-data)Warning: thread-local data

Because `op` is executing within the Rayon thread pool,
thread-local data from the current thread will not be
accessible.

[§](https://docs.rs#warning-execution-order)Warning: execution order

If the current thread is part of a different thread pool, it will try to
keep busy while the `op` completes in its target pool, similar to
calling [ ThreadPool::yield_now()](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html#method.yield_now) in a loop. Therefore, it may
potentially schedule other tasks to run on the current thread in the
meantime. For example

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(1).build_global().unwrap();
    let pool = rayon_core::ThreadPoolBuilder::default().build().unwrap();
    let do_it = || {
        print!("one ");
        pool.install(||{});
        print!("two ");
    };
    rayon::join(|| do_it(), || do_it());
}
```
Since we configured just one thread in the global pool, one might
expect `do_it()` to run sequentially, producing:

`one two one two`However each call to `install()` yields implicitly, allowing rayon to
run multiple instances of `do_it()` concurrently on the single, global
thread. The following output would be equally valid:

`one one two two`[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If `op` should panic, that panic will be propagated.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-install)Using `install()`

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
   fn main() {
        let pool = rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(8).build().unwrap();
        let n = pool.install(|| fib(20));
        println!("{}", n);
   }
   fn fib(n: usize) -> usize {
        if n == 0 || n == 1 {
            return n;
        }
        let (a, b) = rayon::join(|| fib(n - 1), || fib(n - 2)); // runs inside of `pool`
        return a + b;
    }
```
Executes `op` within every thread in the thread pool. Any attempts to use
`join`, `scope`, or parallel iterators will then operate within that
thread pool.

Broadcasts are executed on each thread after they have exhausted their
local work queue, before they attempt work-stealing from other threads.
The goal of that strategy is to run everywhere in a timely manner
*without* being too disruptive to current work. There may be alternative
broadcast styles added in the future for more or less aggressive
injection, if the need arises.

[§](https://docs.rs#warning-thread-local-data-1)Warning: thread-local data

Because `op` is executing within the Rayon thread pool,
thread-local data from the current thread will not be
accessible.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-1)Panics

If `op` should panic on one or more threads, exactly one panic
will be propagated, only after all threads have completed
(or panicked) their own `op`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
   use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
   fn main() {
        let pool = rayon::ThreadPoolBuilder::new().num_threads(5).build().unwrap();
        // The argument gives context, including the index of each thread.
        let v: Vec<usize> = pool.broadcast(|ctx| ctx.index() * ctx.index());
        assert_eq!(v, &[0, 1, 4, 9, 16]);
        // The closure can reference the local stack
        let count = AtomicUsize::new(0);
        pool.broadcast(|_| count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed));
        assert_eq!(count.into_inner(), 5);
   }
```

`num_threads()` method for details[Source](https://docs.rs/rayon-core/1.13.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/rayon_core/thread_pool/mod.rs.html#232)#### pub fn [current_thread_index](https://docs.rs#method.current_thread_index)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>

#### pub fn [current_thread_index](https://docs.rs#method.current_thread_index)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>

If called from a Rayon worker thread in this thread pool,
returns the index of that thread; if not called from a Rayon
thread, or called from a Rayon thread that belongs to a
different thread pool, returns `None`.

The index for a given thread will not change over the thread’s lifetime. However, multiple threads may share the same index if they are in distinct thread pools.

[§](https://docs.rs#future-compatibility-note-1)Future compatibility note

Currently, every thread pool (including the global
thread pool) has a fixed number of threads, but this may
change in future Rayon versions (see [the  num_threads() method
for details](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPoolBuilder.html#method.num_threads)). In that case, the index for a
thread would not change during its lifetime, but thread
indices may wind up being reused if threads are terminated and
restarted.

[Source](https://docs.rs/rayon-core/1.13.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/rayon_core/thread_pool/mod.rs.html#259)#### pub fn [current_thread_has_pending_tasks](https://docs.rs#method.current_thread_has_pending_tasks)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/rayon-core/1.13.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/rayon_core/thread_pool/mod.rs.html#259)

#### pub fn [current_thread_has_pending_tasks](https://docs.rs#method.current_thread_has_pending_tasks)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

Returns true if the current worker thread currently has “local tasks” pending. This can be useful as part of a heuristic for deciding whether to spawn a new task or execute code on the current thread, particularly in breadth-first schedulers. However, keep in mind that this is an inherently racy check, as other worker threads may be actively “stealing” tasks from our local deque.

**Background:** Rayon’s uses a [work-stealing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Work_stealing) scheduler. The
key idea is that each thread has its own [deque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-ended_queue) of
tasks. Whenever a new task is spawned – whether through
`join()`, `Scope::spawn()`, or some other means – that new
task is pushed onto the thread’s *local* deque. Worker threads
have a preference for executing their own tasks; if however
they run out of tasks, they will go try to “steal” tasks from
other threads. This function therefore has an inherent race
with other active worker threads, which may be removing items
from the local deque.

Execute `oper_a` and `oper_b` in the thread pool and return
the results. Equivalent to `self.install(|| join(oper_a, oper_b))`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/rayon-core/1.13.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/rayon_core/thread_pool/mod.rs.html#298-301)

Equivalent to `self.install(|| scope_fifo(...))`.

See also: [the  scope_fifo() function](https://docs.rs/fn.scope_fifo.html).

Spawns an asynchronous task in this thread pool. This task will
run in the implicit, global scope, which means that it may outlast

onto the stack (you will likely need a `move` closure).

will run in the implicit, global scope, which means that it may outlast the
current stack frame – therefore, it cannot capture any references onto the
stack (you will likely need a `move` closure).

Cooperatively yields execution to Rayon.

This is similar to the general [ yield_now()](https://docs.rs/fn.yield_now.html), but only if the current
thread is part of

*this*thread pool.

Returns `Some(Yield::Executed)` if anything was executed, `Some(Yield::Idle)` if
nothing was available, or `None` if the current thread is not part this pool.

# get in num_cpus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/num_cpus/^1.13/fn.get.html

`pub fn get() -> `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)## Expand description

Returns the number of available CPUs of the current system.

This function will get the number of logical cores. Sometimes this is different from the number
of physical cores (See [Simultaneous multithreading on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simultaneous_multithreading)).

This will always return at least `1`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let cpus = num_cpus::get();
if cpus > 1 {
    println!("We are on a multicore system with {} CPUs", cpus);
} else {
    println!("We are on a single core system");
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

This will check [sched affinity](http://www.gnu.org/software/libc/manual/html_node/CPU-Affinity.html) on Linux, showing a lower number of CPUs if the current
thread does not have access to all the computer’s CPUs.

This will also check [cgroups](https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/cgroup-v1/cgroups.txt), frequently used in containers to constrain CPU usage.

---

# get_physical in num_cpus - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/num_cpus/^1.13/fn.get_physical.html

`pub fn get_physical() -> `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)## Expand description

Returns the number of physical cores of the current system.

This will always return at least `1`.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

Physical count is supported only on Linux, mac OS and Windows platforms.
On other platforms, or if the physical count fails on supported platforms,
this function returns the same as [ get()](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html), which is the number of logical
CPUS.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let logical_cpus = num_cpus::get();
let physical_cpus = num_cpus::get_physical();
if logical_cpus > physical_cpus {
    println!("We have simultaneous multithreading with about {:.2} \
              logical cores to 1 physical core.",
              (logical_cpus as f64) / (physical_cpus as f64));
} else if logical_cpus == physical_cpus {
    println!("Either we don't have simultaneous multithreading, or our \
              system doesn't support getting the number of physical CPUs.");
} else {
    println!("We have less logical CPUs than physical CPUs, maybe we only have access to \
              some of the CPUs on our system.");
}
```

# threadpool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/threadpool/latest/target-redirect/threadpool/index.html

## Expand description

A thread pool used to execute functions in parallel.

Spawns a specified number of worker threads and replenishes the pool if any worker threads panic.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#synchronized-with-a-channel)Synchronized with a channel

Every thread sends one message over the channel, which then is collected with the `take()`.

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
let n_workers = 4;
let n_jobs = 8;
let pool = ThreadPool::new(n_workers);
let (tx, rx) = channel();
for _ in 0..n_jobs {
    let tx = tx.clone();
    pool.execute(move|| {
        tx.send(1).expect("channel will be there waiting for the pool");
    });
}
assert_eq!(rx.iter().take(n_jobs).fold(0, |a, b| a + b), 8);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#synchronized-with-a-barrier)Synchronized with a barrier

Keep in mind, if a barrier synchronizes more jobs than you have workers in the pool,
you will end up with a [deadlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadlock)
at the barrier which is [not considered unsafe](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/behavior-not-considered-unsafe.html).

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::sync::{Arc, Barrier};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
// create at least as many workers as jobs or you will deadlock yourself
let n_workers = 42;
let n_jobs = 23;
let pool = ThreadPool::new(n_workers);
let an_atomic = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
assert!(n_jobs <= n_workers, "too many jobs, will deadlock");
// create a barrier that waits for all jobs plus the starter thread
let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(n_jobs + 1));
for _ in 0..n_jobs {
    let barrier = barrier.clone();
    let an_atomic = an_atomic.clone();
    pool.execute(move|| {
        // do the heavy work
        an_atomic.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        // then wait for the other threads
        barrier.wait();
    });
}
// wait for the threads to finish the work
barrier.wait();
assert_eq!(an_atomic.load(Ordering::SeqCst), /* n_jobs = */ 23);
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- `ThreadPool`- `ThreadPool`
- [Thread](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)- Pool
- Abstraction of a thread pool for basic parallelism.

[121](https://docs.rs#121)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[122](https://docs.rs#122)        if self.active {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)            self.shared_data.active_count.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[124](https://docs.rs#124)            if thread::panicking() {
[125](https://docs.rs#125)                self.shared_data.panic_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[126](https://docs.rs#126)            }
[127](https://docs.rs#127)            self.shared_data.no_work_notify_all();
[128](https://docs.rs#128)            spawn_in_pool(self.shared_data.clone())
[129](https://docs.rs#129)        }
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    }

[249](https://docs.rs#249)    ///
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    /// Each thread spawned by this pool will have a 4 MB stack:
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    ///
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    /// ```
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    /// let pool = threadpool::Builder::new()
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    ///     .thread_stack_size(4_000_000)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    ///     .build();
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    ///
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    /// for _ in 0..100 {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    ///     pool.execute(|| {
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    ///         println!("This thread has a 4 MB stack size!");
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    ///     })
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// }
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// ```
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    pub fn thread_stack_size(mut self, size: usize) -> Builder {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        self.thread_stack_size = Some(size);
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        self
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    }
[267](https://docs.rs#267)
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// Finalize the [`Builder`] and build the [`ThreadPool`].
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    ///
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    /// [`Builder`]: struct.Builder.html
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// [`ThreadPool`]: struct.ThreadPool.html
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    ///
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    /// # Examples
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    ///
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// ```
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    /// let pool = threadpool::Builder::new()
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    ///     .num_threads(8)
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    ///     .thread_stack_size(4_000_000)
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    ///     .build();
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    /// ```
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    pub fn build(self) -> ThreadPool {
[282](https://docs.rs#282)        let (tx, rx) = channel::<Thunk<'static>>();
[283](https://docs.rs#283)
[284](https://docs.rs#284)        let num_threads = self.num_threads.unwrap_or_else(num_cpus::get);
[285](https://docs.rs#285)
[286](https://docs.rs#286)        let shared_data = Arc::new(ThreadPoolSharedData {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)            name: self.thread_name,
[288](https://docs.rs#288)            job_receiver: Mutex::new(rx),
[289](https://docs.rs#289)            empty_condvar: Condvar::new(),
[290](https://docs.rs#290)            empty_trigger: Mutex::new(()),
[291](https://docs.rs#291)            join_generation: AtomicUsize::new(0),
[292](https://docs.rs#292)            queued_count: AtomicUsize::new(0),
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            active_count: AtomicUsize::new(0),
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            max_thread_count: AtomicUsize::new(num_threads),
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            panic_count: AtomicUsize::new(0),
[296](https://docs.rs#296)            stack_size: self.thread_stack_size,
[297](https://docs.rs#297)        });
[298](https://docs.rs#298)
[299](https://docs.rs#299)        // Threadpool threads
[300](https://docs.rs#300)        for _ in 0..num_threads {
[301](https://docs.rs#301)            spawn_in_pool(shared_data.clone());
[302](https://docs.rs#302)        }
[303](https://docs.rs#303)
[304](https://docs.rs#304)        ThreadPool {
[305](https://docs.rs#305)            jobs: tx,
[306](https://docs.rs#306)            shared_data: shared_data,
[307](https://docs.rs#307)        }
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)}
[310](https://docs.rs#310)
[311](https://docs.rs#311)struct ThreadPoolSharedData {
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    name: Option<String>,
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    job_receiver: Mutex<Receiver<Thunk<'static>>>,
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    empty_trigger: Mutex<()>,
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    empty_condvar: Condvar,
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    join_generation: AtomicUsize,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    queued_count: AtomicUsize,
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    active_count: AtomicUsize,
[319](https://docs.rs#319)    max_thread_count: AtomicUsize,
[320](https://docs.rs#320)    panic_count: AtomicUsize,
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    stack_size: Option<usize>,
[322](https://docs.rs#322)}
[323](https://docs.rs#323)
[324](https://docs.rs#324)impl ThreadPoolSharedData {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    fn has_work(&self) -> bool {
[326](https://docs.rs#326)        self.queued_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst) > 0 || self.active_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst) > 0
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)
[329](https://docs.rs#329)    /// Notify all observers joining this pool if there is no more work to do.
[330](https://docs.rs#330)    fn no_work_notify_all(&self) {
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        if !self.has_work() {
[332](https://docs.rs#332)            *self
[333](https://docs.rs#333)                .empty_trigger
[334](https://docs.rs#334)                .lock()
[335](https://docs.rs#335)                .expect("Unable to notify all joining threads");
[336](https://docs.rs#336)            self.empty_condvar.notify_all();
[337](https://docs.rs#337)        }
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    }

[344](https://docs.rs#344)    //
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    // This is the only such Sender, so when it is dropped all subthreads will
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    // quit.
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    jobs: Sender<Thunk<'static>>,
[348](https://docs.rs#348)    shared_data: Arc<ThreadPoolSharedData>,
[349](https://docs.rs#349)}

[411](https://docs.rs#411)    /// Executes the function `job` on a thread in the pool.
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    ///
[413](https://docs.rs#413)    /// # Examples
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    ///
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    /// Execute four jobs on a thread pool that can run two jobs concurrently:
[416](https://docs.rs#416)    ///
[417](https://docs.rs#417)    /// ```
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;

[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// pool.execute(|| println!("bar"));
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    /// pool.join();
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// ```
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    pub fn execute<F>(&self, job: F)
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    where
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        F: FnOnce() + Send + 'static,
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    {
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        self.shared_data.queued_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        self.jobs
[433](https://docs.rs#433)            .send(Box::new(job))
[434](https://docs.rs#434)            .expect("ThreadPool::execute unable to send job into queue.");
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    }

[529](https://docs.rs#529)
[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// Sets the number of worker-threads to use as `num_threads`.
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    /// Can be used to change the threadpool size during runtime.
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// Will not abort already running or waiting threads.
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    ///
[534](https://docs.rs#534)    /// # Panics
[535](https://docs.rs#535)    ///
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    /// This function will panic if `num_threads` is 0.
[537](https://docs.rs#537)    ///
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    /// # Examples
[539](https://docs.rs#539)    ///
[540](https://docs.rs#540)    /// ```
[541](https://docs.rs#541)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[542](https://docs.rs#542)    /// use std::time::Duration;
[543](https://docs.rs#543)    /// use std::thread::sleep;
[544](https://docs.rs#544)    ///
[545](https://docs.rs#545)    /// let mut pool = ThreadPool::new(4);
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    /// for _ in 0..10 {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    ///     pool.execute(move || {
[548](https://docs.rs#548)    ///         sleep(Duration::from_secs(100));
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    ///     });
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    /// }
[551](https://docs.rs#551)    ///
[552](https://docs.rs#552)    /// sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for threads to start
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    /// assert_eq!(4, pool.active_count());
[554](https://docs.rs#554)    /// assert_eq!(6, pool.queued_count());
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    ///
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    /// // Increase thread capacity of the pool
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    /// pool.set_num_threads(8);
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    ///
[559](https://docs.rs#559)    /// sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for new threads to start
[560](https://docs.rs#560)    /// assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
[561](https://docs.rs#561)    /// assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
[562](https://docs.rs#562)    ///
[563](https://docs.rs#563)    /// // Decrease thread capacity of the pool
[564](https://docs.rs#564)    /// // No active threads are killed
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    /// pool.set_num_threads(4);
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    ///
[567](https://docs.rs#567)    /// assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    /// assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    /// ```
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    pub fn set_num_threads(&mut self, num_threads: usize) {
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        assert!(num_threads >= 1);
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        let prev_num_threads = self
[573](https://docs.rs#573)            .shared_data
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            .max_thread_count
[575](https://docs.rs#575)            .swap(num_threads, Ordering::Release);
[576](https://docs.rs#576)        if let Some(num_spawn) = num_threads.checked_sub(prev_num_threads) {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)            // Spawn new threads
[578](https://docs.rs#578)            for _ in 0..num_spawn {
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                spawn_in_pool(self.shared_data.clone());
[580](https://docs.rs#580)            }
[581](https://docs.rs#581)        }
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    }
[583](https://docs.rs#583)
[584](https://docs.rs#584)    /// Block the current thread until all jobs in the pool have been executed.
[585](https://docs.rs#585)    ///
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    /// Calling `join` on an empty pool will cause an immediate return.
[587](https://docs.rs#587)    /// `join` may be called from multiple threads concurrently.
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    /// A `join` is an atomic point in time. All threads joining before the join
[589](https://docs.rs#589)    /// event will exit together even if the pool is processing new jobs by the
[590](https://docs.rs#590)    /// time they get scheduled.
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    ///
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    /// Calling `join` from a thread within the pool will cause a deadlock. This
[593](https://docs.rs#593)    /// behavior is considered safe.
[594](https://docs.rs#594)    ///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)    /// # Examples
[596](https://docs.rs#596)    ///
[597](https://docs.rs#597)    /// ```
[598](https://docs.rs#598)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    /// use std::sync::Arc;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)    /// use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
[601](https://docs.rs#601)    ///
[602](https://docs.rs#602)    /// let pool = ThreadPool::new(8);
[603](https://docs.rs#603)    /// let test_count = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
[604](https://docs.rs#604)    ///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)    /// for _ in 0..42 {
[606](https://docs.rs#606)    ///     let test_count = test_count.clone();
[607](https://docs.rs#607)    ///     pool.execute(move || {
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    ///         test_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
[609](https://docs.rs#609)    ///     });
[610](https://docs.rs#610)    /// }
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    ///
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    /// pool.join();
[613](https://docs.rs#613)    /// assert_eq!(42, test_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
[614](https://docs.rs#614)    /// ```
[615](https://docs.rs#615)    pub fn join(&self) {
[616](https://docs.rs#616)        // fast path requires no mutex
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        if self.shared_data.has_work() == false {
[618](https://docs.rs#618)            return ();
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        }
[620](https://docs.rs#620)
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        let generation = self.shared_data.join_generation.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        let mut lock = self.shared_data.empty_trigger.lock().unwrap();
[623](https://docs.rs#623)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)        while generation == self.shared_data.join_generation.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)            && self.shared_data.has_work()
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)            lock = self.shared_data.empty_condvar.wait(lock).unwrap();
[628](https://docs.rs#628)        }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)
[630](https://docs.rs#630)        // increase generation if we are the first thread to come out of the loop
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        self.shared_data.join_generation.compare_and_swap(
[632](https://docs.rs#632)            generation,
[633](https://docs.rs#633)            generation.wrapping_add(1),
[634](https://docs.rs#634)            Ordering::SeqCst,
[635](https://docs.rs#635)        );
[636](https://docs.rs#636)    }
[637](https://docs.rs#637)}
[638](https://docs.rs#638)
[639](https://docs.rs#639)impl Clone for ThreadPool {
[640](https://docs.rs#640)    /// Cloning a pool will create a new handle to the pool.
[641](https://docs.rs#641)    /// The behavior is similar to [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/sync/struct.Arc.html).
[642](https://docs.rs#642)    ///
[643](https://docs.rs#643)    /// We could for example submit jobs from multiple threads concurrently.
[644](https://docs.rs#644)    ///
[645](https://docs.rs#645)    /// ```
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[647](https://docs.rs#647)    /// use std::thread;
[648](https://docs.rs#648)    /// use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
[649](https://docs.rs#649)    ///
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    /// let pool = ThreadPool::with_name("clone example".into(), 2);
[651](https://docs.rs#651)    ///
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    /// let results = (0..2)
[653](https://docs.rs#653)    ///     .map(|i| {
[654](https://docs.rs#654)    ///         let pool = pool.clone();
[655](https://docs.rs#655)    ///         thread::spawn(move || {
[656](https://docs.rs#656)    ///             let (tx, rx) = channel();
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    ///             for i in 1..12 {
[658](https://docs.rs#658)    ///                 let tx = tx.clone();
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    ///                 pool.execute(move || {
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    ///                     tx.send(i).expect("channel will be waiting");
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    ///                 });
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///             }
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    ///             drop(tx);
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    ///             if i == 0 {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    ///                 rx.iter().fold(0, |accumulator, element| accumulator + element)
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    ///             } else {
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    ///                 rx.iter().fold(1, |accumulator, element| accumulator * element)
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    ///             }
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    ///         })
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    ///     })
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    ///     .map(|join_handle| join_handle.join().expect("collect results from threads"))
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    ///     .collect::<Vec<usize>>();
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    ///
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    /// assert_eq!(vec![66, 39916800], results);
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// ```
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    fn clone(&self) -> ThreadPool {
[677](https://docs.rs#677)        ThreadPool {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)            jobs: self.jobs.clone(),
[679](https://docs.rs#679)            shared_data: self.shared_data.clone(),
[680](https://docs.rs#680)        }
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    }
[682](https://docs.rs#682)}
[683](https://docs.rs#683)
[684](https://docs.rs#684)/// Create a thread pool with one thread per CPU.
[685](https://docs.rs#685)/// On machines with hyperthreading,
[686](https://docs.rs#686)/// this will create one thread per hyperthread.
[687](https://docs.rs#687)impl Default for ThreadPool {
[688](https://docs.rs#688)    fn default() -> Self {
[689](https://docs.rs#689)        ThreadPool::new(num_cpus::get())
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    }
[691](https://docs.rs#691)}

[693](https://docs.rs#693)impl fmt::Debug for ThreadPool {

[695](https://docs.rs#695)        f.debug_struct("ThreadPool")
[696](https://docs.rs#696)            .field("name", &self.shared_data.name)
[697](https://docs.rs#697)            .field("queued_count", &self.queued_count())
[698](https://docs.rs#698)            .field("active_count", &self.active_count())
[699](https://docs.rs#699)            .field("max_count", &self.max_count())
[700](https://docs.rs#700)            .finish()
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    }

[704](https://docs.rs#704)impl PartialEq for ThreadPool {
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// Check if you are working with the same pool
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    ///
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// ```
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// use threadpool::ThreadPool;
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    ///
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    /// let a = ThreadPool::new(2);
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// let b = ThreadPool::new(2);
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    ///
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// assert_eq!(a, a);
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// assert_eq!(b, b);
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    ///
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// # // TODO: change this to assert_ne in the future
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    /// assert!(a != b);
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    /// assert!(b != a);
[719](https://docs.rs#719)    /// ```
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    fn eq(&self, other: &ThreadPool) -> bool {
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        let a: &ThreadPoolSharedData = &*self.shared_data;
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        let b: &ThreadPoolSharedData = &*other.shared_data;
[723](https://docs.rs#723)        a as *const ThreadPoolSharedData == b as *const ThreadPoolSharedData
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        // with rust 1.17 and late:
[725](https://docs.rs#725)        // Arc::ptr_eq(&self.shared_data, &other.shared_data)
[726](https://docs.rs#726)    }
[727](https://docs.rs#727)}
[728](https://docs.rs#728)impl Eq for ThreadPool {}
[729](https://docs.rs#729)
[730](https://docs.rs#730)fn spawn_in_pool(shared_data: Arc<ThreadPoolSharedData>) {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    let mut builder = thread::Builder::new();
[732](https://docs.rs#732)    if let Some(ref name) = shared_data.name {
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        builder = builder.name(name.clone());
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    }
[735](https://docs.rs#735)    if let Some(ref stack_size) = shared_data.stack_size {
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        builder = builder.stack_size(stack_size.to_owned());
[737](https://docs.rs#737)    }
[738](https://docs.rs#738)    builder
[739](https://docs.rs#739)        .spawn(move || {
[740](https://docs.rs#740)            // Will spawn a new thread on panic unless it is cancelled.
[741](https://docs.rs#741)            let sentinel = Sentinel::new(&shared_data);
[742](https://docs.rs#742)
[743](https://docs.rs#743)            loop {
[744](https://docs.rs#744)                // Shutdown this thread if the pool has become smaller
[745](https://docs.rs#745)                let thread_counter_val = shared_data.active_count.load(Ordering::Acquire);
[746](https://docs.rs#746)                let max_thread_count_val = shared_data.max_thread_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
[747](https://docs.rs#747)                if thread_counter_val >= max_thread_count_val {
[748](https://docs.rs#748)                    break;
[749](https://docs.rs#749)                }
[750](https://docs.rs#750)                let message = {
[751](https://docs.rs#751)                    // Only lock jobs for the time it takes
[752](https://docs.rs#752)                    // to get a job, not run it.
[753](https://docs.rs#753)                    let lock = shared_data
[754](https://docs.rs#754)                        .job_receiver
[755](https://docs.rs#755)                        .lock()
[756](https://docs.rs#756)                        .expect("Worker thread unable to lock job_receiver");
[757](https://docs.rs#757)                    lock.recv()
[758](https://docs.rs#758)                };
[759](https://docs.rs#759)
[760](https://docs.rs#760)                let job = match message {
[761](https://docs.rs#761)                    Ok(job) => job,
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                    // The ThreadPool was dropped.
[763](https://docs.rs#763)                    Err(..) => break,
[764](https://docs.rs#764)                };
[765](https://docs.rs#765)                // Do not allow IR around the job execution
[766](https://docs.rs#766)                shared_data.active_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[767](https://docs.rs#767)                shared_data.queued_count.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[768](https://docs.rs#768)
[769](https://docs.rs#769)                job.call_box();
[770](https://docs.rs#770)
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                shared_data.active_count.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
[772](https://docs.rs#772)                shared_data.no_work_notify_all();
[773](https://docs.rs#773)            }
[774](https://docs.rs#774)
[775](https://docs.rs#775)            sentinel.cancel();
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        })
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        .unwrap();
[778](https://docs.rs#778)}

[995](https://docs.rs#995)

[997](https://docs.rs#997)        for _ in 0..2 {

[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)    /// The scenario is joining threads should not be stuck once their wave
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)    /// of joins has completed. So once one thread joining on a pool has
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)    /// succeded other threads joining on the same pool must get out even if
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)    /// the thread is used for other jobs while the first group is finishing
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)    /// their join
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)    ///
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)    /// In this example this means the waiting threads will exit the join in
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)    /// groups of four because the waiter pool has four workers.
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)    fn test_join_wavesurfer() {
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)        let n_cycles = 4;
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)        let n_workers = 4;
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)        let (tx, rx) = channel();
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)        let builder = Builder::new()
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)            .num_threads(n_workers)
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)            .thread_name("join wavesurfer".into());
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)        let p_waiter = builder.clone().build();
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)        let p_clock = builder.build();
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)        let barrier = Arc::new(Barrier::new(3));
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)        let wave_clock = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)        let clock_thread = {
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)            let barrier = barrier.clone();
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)            let wave_clock = wave_clock.clone();
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)            thread::spawn(move || {
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)                barrier.wait();
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)                for wave_num in 0..n_cycles {
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)                    wave_clock.store(wave_num, Ordering::SeqCst);
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)                    sleep(Duration::from_secs(1));
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)                }
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)            })
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)        };
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)        {
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)            let barrier = barrier.clone();
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)            p_clock.execute(move || {
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)                barrier.wait();
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)                // this sleep is for stabilisation on weaker platforms
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)                sleep(Duration::from_millis(100));
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)            });
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)        }
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)        // prepare three waves of jobs
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)        for i in 0..3 * n_workers {
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)            let p_clock = p_clock.clone();
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)            let tx = tx.clone();
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)            let wave_clock = wave_clock.clone();
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)            p_waiter.execute(move || {
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)                let now = wave_clock.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)                p_clock.join();
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)                // submit jobs for the second wave
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)                p_clock.execute(|| sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)));
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)                let clock = wave_clock.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)                tx.send((now, clock, i)).unwrap();
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)            });
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)        }
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)        println!("all scheduled at {}", wave_clock.load(Ordering::SeqCst));
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)        barrier.wait();
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)        p_clock.join();
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)        //p_waiter.join();
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)        drop(tx);
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)        let mut hist = vec![0; n_cycles];
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)        let mut data = vec![];
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)        for (now, after, i) in rx.iter() {
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)            let mut dur = after - now;
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)            if dur >= n_cycles - 1 {
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)                dur = n_cycles - 1;
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)            }
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)            hist[dur] += 1;
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)            data.push((now, after, i));
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)        }
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)        for (i, n) in hist.iter().enumerate() {
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)            println!(
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)                "\t{}: {} {}",
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)                i,
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)                n,
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)                &*(0..*n).fold("".to_owned(), |s, _| s + "*")
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)            );
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)        }
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)        assert!(data.iter().all(|&(cycle, stop, i)| if i < n_workers {
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)            cycle == stop
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)        } else {
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)            cycle < stop
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)        }));
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)

# Builder in threadpool - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/threadpool/latest/target-redirect/threadpool/struct.Builder.html

`pub struct Builder { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

[ ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html) factory, which can be used in order to configure the properties of the

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

`ThreadPool`The three configuration options available:

- `num_threads`: maximum number of threads that will be alive at any given moment by the built- `ThreadPool`
- `thread_name`: thread name for each of the threads spawned by the built- `ThreadPool`
- `thread_stack_size`: stack size (in bytes) for each of the threads spawned by the built- `ThreadPool`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Build a [ ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html) that uses a maximum of eight threads simultaneously and each thread has
a 8 MB stack size:

```
let pool = threadpool::Builder::new()
    .num_threads(8)
    .thread_stack_size(8_000_000)
    .build();
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#208-212)#### pub fn [num_threads](https://docs.rs#method.num_threads)(self, num_threads: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#208-212)

#### pub fn [num_threads](https://docs.rs#method.num_threads)(self, num_threads: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)

Set the maximum number of worker-threads that will be alive at any given moment by the built
[ ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html). If not specified, defaults the number of threads to the number of CPUs.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

This method will panic if `num_threads` is 0.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

No more than eight threads will be alive simultaneously for this pool:

```
use std::thread;
let pool = threadpool::Builder::new()
    .num_threads(8)
    .build();
for _ in 0..100 {
    pool.execute(|| {
        println!("Hello from a worker thread!")
    })
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#570-582)#### pub fn [set_num_threads](https://docs.rs#method.set_num_threads)(&mut self, num_threads: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#570-582)

#### pub fn [set_num_threads](https://docs.rs#method.set_num_threads)(&mut self, num_threads: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html))

Sets the number of worker-threads to use as `num_threads`.
Can be used to change the threadpool size during runtime.
Will not abort already running or waiting threads.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

This function will panic if `num_threads` is 0.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::time::Duration;
use std::thread::sleep;
let mut pool = ThreadPool::new(4);
for _ in 0..10 {
    pool.execute(move || {
        sleep(Duration::from_secs(100));
    });
}
sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for threads to start
assert_eq!(4, pool.active_count());
assert_eq!(6, pool.queued_count());
// Increase thread capacity of the pool
pool.set_num_threads(8);
sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)); // wait for new threads to start
assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
// Decrease thread capacity of the pool
// No active threads are killed
pool.set_num_threads(4);
assert_eq!(8, pool.active_count());
assert_eq!(2, pool.queued_count());
```
Block the current thread until all jobs in the pool have been executed.

Calling `join` on an empty pool will cause an immediate return.
`join` may be called from multiple threads concurrently.
A `join` is an atomic point in time. All threads joining before the join
event will exit together even if the pool is processing new jobs by the
time they get scheduled.

Calling `join` from a thread within the pool will cause a deadlock. This
behavior is considered safe.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
let pool = ThreadPool::new(8);
let test_count = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
for _ in 0..42 {
    let test_count = test_count.clone();
    pool.execute(move || {
        test_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    });
}
pool.join();
assert_eq!(42, test_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/threadpool/lib.rs.html#676-681)

[§](https://docs.rs#method.clone)

#### fn [clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone)(&self) -> [ThreadPool](https://docs.rs/struct.ThreadPool.html)

Cloning a pool will create a new handle to the pool.
The behavior is similar to [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/sync/struct.Arc.html).

We could for example submit jobs from multiple threads concurrently.

```
use threadpool::ThreadPool;
use std::thread;
use std::sync::mpsc::channel;
let pool = ThreadPool::with_name("clone example".into(), 2);
let results = (0..2)
    .map(|i| {
        let pool = pool.clone();
        thread::spawn(move || {
            let (tx, rx) = channel();
            for i in 1..12 {
                let tx = tx.clone();
                pool.execute(move || {
                    tx.send(i).expect("channel will be waiting");
                });
            }
            drop(tx);
            if i == 0 {
                rx.iter().fold(0, |accumulator, element| accumulator + element)
            } else {
                rx.iter().fold(1, |accumulator, element| accumulator * element)
            }
        })
    })
    .map(|join_handle| join_handle.join().expect("collect results from threads"))
    .collect::<Vec<usize>>();
assert_eq!(vec![66, 39916800], results);
```

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

CLI Helpers
